answer:
Given matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$.

Perform elementary row operations to reduce $A$ to Echelon form:

1. Apply $R_2 \to R_2 - 2R_1$ and $R_3 \to R_3 - 3R_1$:
$$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 7 & -7 & 6 \end{bmatrix}$|

2. Apply $R_3 \to 3R_3 - 7R_2$:
$$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -10 \end{bmatrix}$|
This upper triangular form is the **Echelon form** of the matrix. The number of non-zero rows is $3$, so **$\text{Rank}(A) = 3$**.

---

**Row Reduced Echelon Form (RREF):**

3. Make leading entries $1$ and clear columns:
Divide $R_3$ by $7$ ($R_3 \to \frac{1}{7}R_3$):
$$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 3 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -10/7 \end{bmatrix}$|

4. Apply $R_1 \to R_1 - 3R_3$ and $R_2 \to R_2 + 4R_3$:
$$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 0 & 23/7 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -12/7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -10/7 \end{bmatrix}$|

5. Divide $R_2$ by $3$ ($R_2 \to \frac{1}{3}R_2$):
$$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 0 & 23/7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -4/7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -10/7 \end{bmatrix}$|

6. Apply $R_1 \to R_1 + 2R_2$:
$$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & 15/7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -4/7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -10/7 \end{bmatrix}$|
This is the **Row Reduced Echelon Form (RREF)**.
proTip: The rank of a matrix equals the number of non-zero rows in its Echelon form. Always verify your pivot elements.
